title: Few-Shot & Chain-of-Thought
motto: Telling a model what to do is prompting. Showing it how to think is engineering. The gap between 78% and 91% accuracy on the same model, same task, same data is not a better model. It is a better reasoning strategy.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Telling a model what to do is prompting. Showing it how to think is engineering. The gap between 78% and 91% accuracy on the same model, same task, same data is not a better model. It is a better reasoning strategy.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: You build a math tutoring app. Your prompt says: "Solve this word problem." GPT-5 gets it right 94% of the time on GSM8K, the standard grade-school math benchmark. You think you already peaked. You do not — chain-of-thought still adds 3-4 points.

Add five words -- "Let's think step by step" -- and accuracy jumps to 91%. Add a few worked examples and it reaches 95%. Same model. Same temperature. Same API cost. The only difference is that you gave the model scratch paper.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: Show examples in the prompt (few-shot). Ask the model to think step-by-step (CoT) before the final answer.

steps.title: Implement cot
steps.body: Write the function from scratch in the workspace. Run when ready — all tests must pass.
